question: An anaesthetist draws up propofol correctly but accidentally injects it into a drip line that is not running, so the patient receives none. Which type of error is this?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A mistake occurs when the plan itself is wrong. Here the plan (propofol IV induction) was correct; the execution failed.

answers.text: Slip — an error of execution with a correct plan

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A slip is an error of execution where the intended action is correct but is performed incorrectly. The plan (propofol induction) was sound; the technical action (injecting into a running line) failed.

answers.text: Violation — a deliberate deviation from a safe practice

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A violation is intentional non-compliance with a known rule. This was an unintentional technical error, not a deliberate deviation.

answers.text: Near miss — an event that caused no harm and requires no further analysis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A near miss is a valid safety concept, but it describes the outcome (harm avoided), not the type of error. The error type here is a slip.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the error taxonomy: slips = right plan, wrong execution; mistakes = wrong plan. This scenario had a correct plan executed incorrectly, so it is a slip.
Correct. Slips are errors of execution — the right plan, wrong action. Recognising the error type guides the appropriate prevention strategy.
